findings.reason: the same summary has driven a coordinator dispatch at already-landed work twice before, and a reader who trusts "§8–§15" never sees §16 queued.
findings.text: the intro states "§8–§15 are follow-ons from their reviews", but §16 is a fifth follow-on, from §10's review (the §10 landing comment at line 332 names it: "The consolidation follow-on is §16"), so the plan's summary of its follow-on set omits one of its own sections

findings.reason: following the open followup redispatches completed work, and leaving §16 outside the one-at-a-time ordering lets a coordinator dispatch it concurrently with §14 onto one module.
findings.text: the only open followup `f-lmr-008` is titled "Build §10, then §14; build §15" and carries `data-recommends-skill="/reckon-build lane-and-model-routing §10"`, but §10 landed at merge `0e4b8adba` (line 332) and §15 at `e75f1b406` (line 323), and the followup never names §16 although §16 edits `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`, the same module §14 edits and the followup serialises only for §10/§14

findings.reason: the mechanism "make the other two call it" is undefined for a project-to-repository function, so an implementer consolidating the wrong site will either break `project_mount_repository` or discover the done-when cannot be written.
findings.text: §16 states `_repository_owning_projects` "is the third spelling of the repository-to-projects resolution, beside one in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and one in `reckon/crew/dispatch_sections.py`", but the `reckon/crew/dispatch_sections.py` site (`project_mount_repository`, line 49) resolves a project to its repository — the inverse direction — and takes no path, so it can neither "disagree ... about a worktree path" (the next sentence's premise) nor "name the same projects"

findings.reason: a measure that cannot be taken against one of its three named inputs leaves §16's gate unable to show the consolidation it asks for.
findings.text: §16's done-when asserts "a test passes a linked worktree of a mounted repository to each of the three call sites and shows they name the same projects", but one of the three named call sites takes a project name and returns a repository root, so the described test cannot be constructed for it and the "at least one site does not name them" negative control cannot be evaluated

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the design report, `reckon/_backends.py` `_DIALECTS`, and §16's three cited modules all resolve; extensionless archive hrefs resolve as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's done-when (line 120) requires a linked worktree to be passed to each of three call sites that "name the same projects", but one of the three named sites does not resolve a repository to projects.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — cited evidence sits under `docs/evidence/archive/lane-and-model-routing-landed.html` and `docs/evidence/fragments/lane-and-model-routing/`, both present and durable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new §16 and the amended intro carry no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — the intro's follow-on set is one section short of the plan's own section list (line 42), and §16's premise that the `dispatch_sections.py` site is a repository-to-projects resolution is not what that code does (line 120).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16 names one deliverable (one repository-to-projects owner), and the amended document content keeps each node on one goal.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the only open followup `f-lmr-008` (line 202) points its prompt at §10, which the plan records as done at merge `0e4b8adba` (line 332), and omits §16.
